title: Maximum Power Transfer: Match the Load to the Source
topic: Maximum power transfer theorem — a source with internal resistance R_s delivers the most power into a load R_L when R_L equals R_s; the load power P_L = V_s²·R_L/(R_s+R_L)² peaks at R_L = R_s with value V_s²/(4R_s) and efficiency 50%

beats.narration: What load pulls the most power out of a source?

elements.content: What load pulls the most power out of a source?

beats.narration: A real source has an internal resistance R sub s. The current through any load R sub L equals V sub s divided by R sub s plus R sub L. The power delivered into the load is I squared times R sub L.

elements.content: Circuit: V_s in series with R_s, terminals labelled, R_L drawn as variable resistor with arrow

beats.narration: Sweep the load from very small to very large. With a tiny load, the current is huge but the load voltage is nearly zero — almost no power. With a huge load, the voltage is full but the current is nearly zero — also almost no power. The peak sits in the middle.

elements.content: Horizontal axis: R_L from 0 to 4·R_s; vertical axis: P_L (normalised)
Power curve P_L(R_L) traces left-to-right as R_L sweeps
Slider on the R_L axis and corresponding (R_L, P_L) marker on the curve, peak at R_L = R_s
Dashed vertical line at R_L = R_s with peak callout
the peak sits where the load matches the source

beats.narration: At the peak the load equals R sub s, and the delivered power is V sub s squared over four R sub s. Half the source energy goes to the load, half is wasted in R sub s — fifty percent efficiency at maximum power transfer.

elements.content: efficiency at the peak: fifty percent
half the source energy heats R_s

beats.narration: Match the load when you want maximum power — useful for antennas and signal receivers, wasteful for power distribution.

elements.content: (great for receivers, terrible for the grid)
